thread:
IncidentBot: ALERT: spike in tool/function-call queue length + malformed structured-output errors across hosted cluster us-east-1. Error rate on fn-invoke path > 12% last 5m, tail latency > 2s. Paging oncall.
Sara: oncall here, looking. Any idea which customer signals are driving this?
Mike: seeing a huge surge from a few API keys doing function-heavy chat + streaming structured JSON. They’re hitting continuous tool invocations per request.
Raj: yep, same. KV cache pressure + many long sequences, runtime keeps flushing caches and exhausting GPU memory shards -> retries + backpressure.
Elaine: impact: some requests return 5xx, others timeout mid-stream. Customers on hosted free tier mainly but we’re seeing retries hit dedicated pools as well via fallback routing.
Tom: suggestion: short-term mitigation = 1) throttle fn-call rate per key 2) disable structured JSON streaming (switch to plain text) 3) increase gateway token-level rate-limits for suspected keys. We can do 1 and 2 quickly via feature flags.
Sara: agreed. Prioritize disabling structured output streaming first? That will reduce parsing/validation and drop KV cache churn.
Mike: disabling structured streaming reduces CPU + serialization pressure. But function calls are main consumer of external tool backends; still need to cap.
Raj: I can push a policy to edge to limit fn-call concurrency per key to 2 and total rate to 10req/s for flagged keys. Rollout to us-east-1 only first.
Elaine: I’ll flip the structured-output flag to "compact" mode (server-side) which falls back to line-delimited text instead of full JSON streaming. Command:

```
# flip feature flag for hosted tier (us-east-1 only)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://admin.redwood/api/flags/structured_output -d '{"mode":"compact","region":"us-east-1"}'
```

Mike: I’ll run the fn-call concurrency policy change on the gateway:

```
# create short-lived policy
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://admin.redwood/api/routing/policies -d '{"selector":"keys:[abc123,def456]","fn_call_max_concurrency":2,"region":"us-east-1","note":"emergency throttle 1834567890"}'
```

Raj: deploying policy now.
Tom: I’ll prepare rollback steps. Rollback plan: remove policy + set structured_output back to "streaming". Keep canary window 5m between steps.
Sara: runbook update: set status page to "degraded performance" for hosted generation API and mention we are restricting function calls and structured streaming to mitigate. @ops-team please post.
Elaine: status update posted to status.redwood: "Investigating; temporarily limiting tool/function calls and changing structured output to compact. Some users may see degraded streaming or fewer tool invocations."
IncidentBot: NOTE: page created 1834567890, severity P2. Oncall owner: Sara. Follow runbook: emergency throttle -> notify customers -> monitor for 30m -> escalate to SRE lead if errors persist.
Mike: policy applied. Gateway returns 200 for policy creation. I’ll attach the policy id: pol-83a2. Observability: fn-invoke attempts per second dropped ~60% in the flagged keys.
Raj: structured_output flip applied and propagated to proxies. Confirming fallback format in logs: "structured_output=compact"
Sara: seeing error rate drop to 3% and tail latency down to 700ms across the cluster. Good signal.
Tom: keep the policy active for 30 minutes, then we can slowly relax if stable. Engineering action items: 1) schedule deeper root-cause (runtime cache pressure), 2) add adaptive token-aware batching, 3) add better per-key fn-call caps at API layer.
Elaine: customer comms: ops posted to customers-involved thread. Also DM-ing top 3 api-key owners asking them to reduce tool-heavy loops. cc @support to triage any tickets.
Mike: quick note — enabling compact mode removed JSON schema validation on stream; make sure we capture a subset of validation errors to avoid silent regressions.
Raj: logging: added temporary extra logs for fn-call failures with sample_id and key; will expire after incident.
Sara: can we get a brief postmortem id? Tom, can you take lead? Capture timeline, decisions, and mitigation efficacy.
Tom: I’ll own the postmortem. Draft due EOD today. I’ll include metrics + dashboard links.
Elaine: removing emergency policy now would be premature. Recommend 30m watch and then staged rollback.
IncidentBot: REMINDER: please add reactions for acknowledgement. :loud_sound: :white_check_mark:
Mike: adding follow-up ticket to eng-runtime: TKT-891 for cache eviction optimizations.
Sara: great work team. Keep the thread updated here. If error rate climbs, we escalate to P1 and widen mitigations.
Tom: monitoring window passed 30m. Error rate stable. I’ll start staged relaxation: increase concurrency to 4, then to 8 after 10m if stable.
Mike: relaxation step 1 applied. No regression.
Sara: thanks — closing active mitigation. Leaving notes in incident tracker and postmortem in #postmortems.
Elaine: final: customers notified, no data loss, degraded UX for some streaming clients. Closing thread.
